selections.comment: Aidan O'Brien's BEAUTIFY can improve from her debut third at the Curragh where she lost her place at the halfway stage and kept on nicely in the closing stages. She is a half-sister to a Listed winner and holds a Group 2 entry in the Curragh at the end of June. Night Of Thunder filly Skydance holds the same Group 2 engagement, so she should be monitored for market strength ahead of her debut. There was promise in Havana Anna's third on racecourse bow at Navan, while Moyglare filly Suzie Songs could show up well on her first outing for Ger Lyons. O'Brien's Closely was easy to back in sixth at Listowel, but shouldn't be ruled out.

He got off the mark in a Gowran Park maiden in May and the form was endorsed when the runner-up came out and took a good handicap in the Curragh. Storm Piece had some notable placed form as a juvenile and appeals as a horse with plenty of upside. Curragh runner-up Pinar Del Rio has a shot of overturning form with the winner, Goal Exceeded, on these terms. Fort Vega finished well for second in Leopardstown and ought to be in the hunt off the same mark. Kings Time has the form to be a factor, but the forecast rain isn't in his favour.

He made the frame in all three starts during the last campaign and his runner-up spot in Navan last summer reads well after the winner followed up in a handicap off a mark of 87. Asdana was a solid third in a Navan handicap last weekend which brings her into contention, while Glory To Be was fourth on debut at the Curragh and will be eyeing prize money. This Ain't Texas is a potential improver.

Killavia ran well on debut over the 6-furlong trip at Haydock last time, and the form of that race looks decent with the winner potentially being a Royal Ascot horse and the 3rd-placed horse coming out and winning since. Alasrae looks to be the best of the newcomers for a yard who do pretty well with their two-year-old runners.

selections.comment: DIAMOND DREAMER has been running very well at present, with a win at Chelmsford in March over this 5-furlong trip; he was always keeping on very well in the closing stages at that course last time out when finishing 2nd in the end. Given the way he ran last time out there, it looks like more to come, and given the stiff nature of the finish at Sandown, the track is sure to suit. All Ways Glamorous has been in fine fettle recently with two wins and a 2nd; he is pretty lightly raced, so he might lack the know-how compared to a few of these. Bang On The Bell is another one going well at present, and he could go well here to fill the placings.

selections.comment: SABA DESERT looks to have plenty of class and potential in his locker, and given the fact he is a well-bred middle-distance type, this relatively testing 7 furlongs will more than suit him. Hailing from a top yard who do so very well with their first-time-out horses, it will be interesting to see how this son of Dubawi gets on here. Boiling Over could only manage a 5th placed effort of 8 runners when a little keen on debut at Haydock last time out. He will be sure to put that experience to good use for another top yard who do well with their youngsters. Waterford Castle looks smart on paper and could fill the placings here before progressing.

selections.comment: CHATURANGA was hanging left when running in this grade in the closing stages at Redcar last time out, and although that was the case, he still managed to finish a decent 3rd in the end. Connections put the blinkers on him this time around, which could rectify that problem, and if it does so, then he is the one to beat here, just 3 lbs higher than his last winning mark. Due to Henry did disappointment last time out at Kempton, however, that was his first run in almost 7 months, so he is entitled to come on for the experience. Back down in trip to 1m2f now, which was the trip when he last won, he could go well here. Promethean was well fancied in his last run, and that would have been for a reason; therefore, he is one to keep an eye on here.

selections.comment: MISS JUSTICE has been slightly frustrating in her last two runs when coming 2nd; however, she did lose her hind right shoe when odds-on favourite last time out at Wolverhampton. She is bred to appreciate this trip, and the opening mark of 82 could prove to be lenient for the daughter of Justify, who is sure to be still improving with each passing run for the Gosdens. William Buick is booked to ride which is an excellent move from connections, and we could finally see her get her head in front here. Kind Of Kiss is a very lightly raced sort who was once owned by Godolphin and trained by Andre Fabre, so there is clearly some talent in there, he could go well here. Approval is a nice type but has to give a bit of weight to some unexposed types in this race; therefore, he can run well and finish in the placings.

selections.comment: Richard Hannon's ANTELOPE landed the double in fine style last time out at Leicester, and the stiff finish of Sandown is sure to suit his runner here. Sean Levey takes control of the reins now as the horse looks to land the hat trick, and with just the 6 lb rise in the weights to deal with here, there is sure to be more to come from this lad. Best Adventure was a winner over the 1m2f trip at Newmarket two runs ago, and the step up in trip to 1m4f probably did not suit the Andrew Balding horse last time out. Sir William is currently a maiden in six career runs, but he ran well to finish 3rd last time out, and there could be more improvement to come from him with Tom Marquand taking the reins now.

The time before that he was a pretty impressive winner at Kempton, and if he can replicate that form here, he is the one they have to beat. Last Shamardal takes an ease in class here, dropping back down to class 5 company for the first time since his last win 3 runs ago; that will more than suit him here. And Miss Collada ran very well in a big field race at York last time; he is another one taking an ease in class here today.

selections.comment: SYNERGISM improved significantly when stepped up in trip this season for Sir Mark Prescott, and given his record for these types who seemingly improve for a step up in trip, there should be more to come from this lad here. Stepping up to the 1m6f for the very first time could bring even more out of this lad, and given the way he seems to do all his running at the same speed, this test should really suit him here. King Kernow has placed 2nd in the last four of his runs, so he has been running well at present, and with Rossa Ryan onboard here, I can see him getting into the places again here. Hi Ya Mal was a nice enough winner last time out but might have to settle for a placed finish here.

selections.comment: Last year's winner, Tolstoy, is three from three over course and distance and would usually be first port of call given he's back below his last wining mark but he's failed to fire in three runs this year and so reluctantly he's overlooked. THE CARIBBEAN could be the answer having kicked off this campaign in good fashion with a placed effort on fast ground over 6f. The step back up to 7f will suit and this might be another step towards rediscovering fomer levels (when trained in Ireland in 2023). Heading a host of dangers are Leap Day, whose been knocking on the door of late and Little Empire, a winner last time out over 7f at Ayr on fast ground and still steadily improving, with marginal preference for the former

selections.comment: This looks a decent opportunity for WILLOWINGHURN to land a double having opened her account on second run at Redcar on fast ground. She just about sets the bar and a repeat of that run could prove enough again, especially given the trio of newcomers don't appear to offer much threat on paper (market support for any would be interesting). The toughest opposition is likely to come from U Turn, who has pretty solid form in the context of this race and could show a bit more for the step up in trip, and Lina Codina, who failed to build on the promise of a decent debut last time but was very poorly drawn and best excused that effort

selections.comment: A very trappy affair with a whole host of possible improvers. Top of the list to consider is RANEENN, proven in handicap company having scored last time on handicap bow following a couple of respectable runs in Listed events and holding solid claims to add a fourth career victory on just her seventh start. Pelean, who improved markedly for the drop back to 6f on fourth start to spring a shock and land a decent novice last time, is interesting first time in a handicap off an opening mark of 78. That looks generous, and if able to hold a handy position early she can go close. Lady Of Andros and Glamour Show are closely matched (the latter is 2lb better off for under a length and was less favourably drawn at Chester last time) and have decent claims but Easy Peeler is perhpas a little more solid having progressed with each run and getting close returned from a layoff to kick off this campaign when placed at Haydock in late May. There should be a fair bit more to come on just her fifth start. Mostar Dreams is another worthy of serious consideration

selections.comment: A high quality affair with plenty arriving in peak form and a few lurking on threatening marks if rediscovering their sparkle. The one to stand out is BURRITO who landed a competitive class 3 event to kick off this campaign last time on handicap bow. A 10lb rise for a narrow margin success may seem steep but the manner of the victory was impressive given how seetly he travelled and then picked up nicely when challenged late by Sovereign Sea (2lb better off for half a length) and was well in command at the line looking as if there was a fair bit left in the locker. The second then should go well again but will struggle to reverse placings off the slightly better terms. He still gets second choice. The progressive Sea That Strom can't be ignored given his extraordinary improvement continued despite defeat last time (by a nose) when just falling shy of recording a five-timer. However, a further four pound rise in this company will be hard to defy and Austrian Theory may offer a bit better value to hit the frame. He has to be excused a tame effort last time over course and distance but is prone to the odd blow-out and could get very competitve if replicating his first two runs this term. Zain Blue is another that merits consideration and has each way claims at a price

He lost his way for much of last term but was placed off 85 when firing in the spring. The possible fast ground is a worry but he has some fair form on it from limited runs and it's worth chancing he can improve on recent efforts to score again. The admirably consistent Gincident is next on the list having proved his stamina for this trip the last twice (a win and placing). Unlike the selection he relishes quick ground and can expolit any vulnerabilities of the selection on that count. Shimmering Sands may be a bit overlooked in the market and has decent each way claims if building on an encouraging season return and can hold off other key contenders such as Pol Roger and Molinari
